explanation: Fires on many different nouns and word pieces in all kinds of text (prose, biomedical writing, code), e.g. 'element', 'offences', 'Treatment', 'content', 'Extension'. There is no shared meaning or context that would predict when it fires.

Fires on various tokens in evaluative or argumentative writing, most often legal opinions ('did not err in', 'affirm the finding', 'trial court has') and opinionated comments addressed to someone ('you don't', 'you guys really'). It is weak on neutral expository text. Several examples (JSON colors, LaTeX) fit no pattern.

Fires on the function word right after a verb or noun that requires a particular preposition or article: 'believe [in]', 'in contrast [to]', 'compared [to]', 'inspired [by]', 'criticised [for]', 'indicate [a]', 'injection [of]'. 'believe in' and 'contrast to' fire most strongly. It is weak on other tokens.

Fires in text about public access to places and visitors: 'residents [and] visitors', 'close/opened [to] public', 'closed [to] traffic', and words like 'tourist', 'visitor', 'attract', 'visiting'. A second, weaker pattern is web/server traffic and counts of views ('has [been] seen', redirect, forwards, log_format).
Fires on a wide variety of tokens (verbs like 'has'/'have'/'had', possessives, name pieces, adjectives such as 'genetic'/'psychological', code punctuation) with no clear common context.

Mainly fires on 'is' right after a sentence-initial question word 'What' ('What [is] the...'), including in math word problems, and on similar words that continue a question or relative clause ('What [on] earth', 'many of [which]'). It also fires on some code tokens and weakly on pieces inside long words.

Fires on 'then' (or Russian 'то') that opens the main clause after an 'if' clause ('If X, [then] Y'), in prose, math and code ('if ... then' in Lua). Sentence-initial 'Then' used for sequence is moderate, and other connectives are weak.

Fires on words that point the reader to where information can be found: 'can be [found] [in] the LICENSE file', 'For details, [see]', 'as you can [see]', 'article [listed] above', 'ask [in] the comments', 'reasons pointed [out]'. It is strongest in license headers in source code.

Fires on a scattered mix of tokens: suffixes of words ('-com[edy]', 'P[.S]'), abbreviations in credit lines ('AP Photo', 'Getty Images/BBC'), code keywords ('package', 'end', 'Promise'), and pronouns or function words. There is no consistent theme.

Fires on pieces in the middle or at the end of rare proper nouns, acronyms and non-English or foreign words that the tokenizer splits up (e.g. 'PAC[AP]', 'Pap[io]', 'Analy[tica]', 'Chab[ot]', 'Khach[an]ov'), and on some preprocessor/code tokens ('defined'). It is weak on ordinary English words.
Fires on a broad mix of nouns and connectives ('or', 'and', 'episode', 'variable', 'object', 'location', 'notice') in technical, scientific and code text. There is no clear shared meaning.
Fires on 'be' after a modal or 'to' ('can [be]', 'shall [be]', 'will [be]', 'going to [be]', 'should [be]'). It is moderate on 'been' after 'have' and weak on 'to' or other verbs in similar slots.

Fires on the argument token right after an opening parenthesis or bracket in code and math, e.g. 'resolve[(file])', 'g[(x])', 'sin[ x]', 'get_class($[this])', 'LinkedList[<Item]>'. It fires when the token is inside nested parentheses or brackets, just before the closing one.

Fires on a mixture: boilerplate in license and copyright headers ('All [rights] reserved', 'without limitation the [rights]', comment-box closers '*/', 'You [should] have received'), 'opened [up]', and various unrelated words.

Fires in text about making decisions or choices: 'make' or 'making' in 'make informed choices / decisions', 'make the [right]/[wrong] decision/call', 'crucial decisions', and on 'before' in 'consider ... before'. It is strongest on 'make' when 'decision' or 'choice' follows.

Fires on the first word pieces of non-English proper names (places, organizations, people), especially South Asian and Middle Eastern ones ('Dou'ma, 'Samajw[adi]', 'Peoples' Party, 'Muj[ah]ideen', 'Das[ht]'), and on pieces of uncommon split-up technical words ('gnot[ob]iotic', 'intr[ab]ody').

Fires on distinctive content words or name pieces: political conflict groups or places ('Donetsk', 'Hezbollah', 'Hamas', 'WikiLeaks', 'riots'), package names after 'import'/'org.' in code ('.jetbrains', '.slf4j', 'shutil', 'timedelta'), and emotionally charged words ('tantrum', 'procrastination', 'desperately').

Fires on the last digit of years in copyright notices ('Copyright (c) 201[2]') and on various tech or spec tokens ('VPS', '375[W]', '1 GB [of]', 'www-data', 'branch'). There are also unrelated scientific word pieces and other words.

Fires on early word pieces of uncommon multi-token words, mostly scientific terms ('Maxwell-[B]oltzmann', 'ant[io]xygenic', '[o]ocyte', '[o]phthalmology', 'pl[as]minogen'), and on non-English words (Italian, Norwegian, Swedish, German).

Mainly fires on the start of citation markers in scientific text: the '@' after '([' or '\[' in references like '([@B12])', and the digits inside reference IDs ('bib0[0]20'). It also fires on p-values ('[p] = 0.') and some other scattered nouns.

Fires on abstract nouns and quantifiers in discourse-framing phrases ('the [choice]', 'the only [difference]', 'an important [challenge]', 'our [aim]', 'two [ways]', 'no [reason]', 'the end [of]', 'most [of]', '[all] of them'). It responds to a word that introduces the claim that follows, but the trigger is diffuse.
